title: Service failure ontology and trace-sampling playbook
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Create a canonical failure ontology for inference-path errors (timeouts, overload, model runtime faults, HTTP/gRPC status mapping) and deliver an operational playbook that ties trace sampling and metric/log pipelines into a unified error dashboard. This ticket covers: 1) taxonomy definition and canonical span/tags for all common failure modes, 2) trace sampling strategy to ensure both signal and low-cardinality tail events are captured, 3) log/metric pipeline transformations and enrichment rules, and 4) a working dashboard and runbook for on-call. The deliverable should reduce time-to-detect and time-to-root-cause for end-to-end inference failures.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical failure ontology documented in Confluence with examples for each class (timeout, overload, model-error, HTTP/gRPC code mapping)
Instrumented trace hooks deployed in runtime (entry/exit/kv-cache) with agreed span tags: service, route, model.version, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, rpc_status, model_error_code
Trace sampling configured: 1% baseline + deterministic sampling for high-latency spans + 100% sampling for spans with rpc_status >= 500 or model_error_code != OK
Log/metric pipeline enrichment implemented (Vector pipeline): map model_error_code to human-friendly labels + attach trace_id, route, and token_latency buckets
New dashboard published in Console with panels for: global failure heatmap, per-route latency P50/P95/P99, overload queue length, model error rate by variant, and HTTP/gRPC error breakdown
On-call playbook added to runbook with triage steps, common remediation actions, and links to related runbooks and PRs
Dashboard has synthetic traffic test showing expected panels populate; incident drill completed once in staging
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive sampling increases costs. We chose deterministic sampling for tail latencies and rule-based 100% capture of error spans to keep cost bounded while preserving debugability.

We intentionally do not change production default sampling yet — this rollout will be canaryed on a subset of routes (low-traffic non-customer critical routes) and evaluated for cost and signal quality.

Model errors: normalize internal model runtime errors (OOM, NaN logits, decode-failure) into a small set of standardized model_error_code values. Avoid leaking raw stack traces into logs by attaching summary codes and safe metadata only.
